decision: a barbell draws the plates for one side after its bar weight, as in 20 kg bar then 15 and 5, from the same plate sizes as the dumbbells, with plates 3 dp narrower on each side
why: the owner lifts the barbell at home with the same plates and asked why it showed none; the narrower plates let six a side fit, so every load up to 155 kg on a 20 kg bar fits the weight row at normal text size
evidence: real-font test in test/render_screens_test.dart stepping a barbell from 20 to 155 kg, a probe up to 200 kg (first overflow at 157.5 kg, seven plates), renders kept outside the repo

decision: the plates dialog picks sizes instead of counting pieces, each size standing for as many as a lift needs, and migration 5 drops plate.pieces keeping every size counted
why: the owner said he does not need plate counts; sizes are still needed, because a usual gym set would draw 20 and 25 kg plates he lacks and never his 1 and 2 kg ones
evidence: test/store_test.dart migrates a v4 file built from test/schema_v4.sql, test/day_test.dart checks the solver against an exhaustive search up to 40 kg

decision: plate counts come back as optional: each owned size has a count or none, a counted size limits each end to its share and an uncounted one is used as often as it takes; migration 6 brings plate.pieces back as nullable and every size from v5 comes back uncounted
why: the owner first said he did not need counts, then wanted them kept once told that without counts the app would draw four 15s a side when he owns two, and proposed counts that apply only when entered; the counts 0.6.0 stored were dropped by the shipped migration 5 and cannot be recovered in the database, only from the .v4.bak copy
evidence: test/store_test.dart migrates v4 and v5 files, test/day_test.dart checks the solver with mixed counts against an exhaustive search, a render of the dialog kept outside the repo
